Production-ready.meaning: Structured field or verified Tagger tag. Safe to run unattended.

Review.meaning: Works, but wording-sensitive or coverage-bounded. Run it, but surface the row's `blind` text to the user so they know what it misses.

Semantic.meaning: Subjective or composite. Never auto-run as an answer; offer it as a starting point a human narrows. Usually needs 2-4 named lenses instead.

Do-not-emit.meaning: Recorded only so the anti-pattern is documented. Never execute.

parameter_guide.[COLORS]: WUBRG letters for the deck's colour identity, e.g. 'ug'. Bind before use.
parameter_guide.[MV]: Mana value threshold. Never infer a 'cheap' threshold silently.
parameter_guide.[TYPE]: Any card type, supertype or subtype.
parameter_guide.[SUBTYPE]: A subtype, usually a creature type.
parameter_guide.[KEYWORD]: A real keyword ability. Ability words are NOT valid with kw:.
parameter_guide.[CARD NAME]: Exact card name for ! searches and membership probes.
parameter_guide.[RANK]: EDHREC rank threshold. Higher number = less played.
parameter_guide.[DATE]: yyyy-mm-dd, a set code, or now.
parameter_guide.[TAG]: An allowlisted Tagger tag only. Never invent one.
parameter_guide.[BASE_QUERY]: Whatever query is under test, for membership probes.
parameter_guide.[REFERENCE_CARD]: A named card to decompose into traits.

caveats: A live_count is the pool size on the validated date, measured with the widest parameter binding. Treat it as an upper bound, not an answer.
Counts drift. Oracle templating changes break text queries silently - that is how Atlas V1 died. Re-run src/build.py after any major Magic release.
Absence of a card from a count is NOT proof of exclusion. To prove membership run: <query> !"Card Name"
Scryfall silently ignores tokens it does not recognise, so never hand-edit a query and assume it still works. Re-run src/run_verify.py after edits.
Validity is proven; semantic correctness is not. A query can be valid and still mean the wrong thing, which is what the tier gating protects against.

rows.label: Commander deck card pool (the default baseline)
rows.blind_spot: Legality in the format is not legality in your deck's identity - both filters are needed. GOV-14.
rows.assumption: [COLORS] is your commander's identity, normalized to WUBRG letters.

rows.label: Exact identity instead of ceiling (only when the user says exactly/only)
rows.blind_spot: Excludes mono-color and colorless cards inside your colors, which are usually wanted.
rows.assumption: Reserved for explicit 'exactly' / 'only these colors' wording.

rows.label: Cards that can be your commander (command-zone eligibility)
rows.blind_spot: is:commander is eligibility, not format legality. They are different questions.

rows.label: Commanders of an exact identity, most-played first
rows.blind_spot: Popularity is not quality. GOV-15.
rows.assumption: order:edhrec ranks by play rate; lower rank number is more played.

rows.label: Commanders that could play a card of given colors
rows.blind_spot: Returns commanders with extra colors too, which is usually the point.

rows.label: No format filter unless the format is actually established
rows.blind_spot: Adding f:commander here would invent context the user did not give.
rows.assumption: Use when the request names colors but never establishes Commander.

rows.label: Printed color, not identity, when the user means the card's own color
rows.blind_spot: Says nothing about what deck the card is legal in.

rows.label: Printed color inside a deck identity (two different constraints)
rows.blind_spot: Add f:commander only when Commander is explicit or in session context.
rows.assumption: 'mono black cards for my golgari deck' - the card is mono-black AND legal in BG.

rows.label: Colorless printed cards vs no color identity
rows.blind_spot: c=c (printed colorless) and id=c (no color identity) answer different questions.

rows.label: Commander-legal cards with no color identity
rows.blind_spot: Includes basic and utility lands. Keep them in search truth; suppress in recommendations only. CAL-046.

rows.label: Either of two colors but not multicolor
rows.blind_spot: Not the same as colors<=1, which also admits colorless. See Open_Decisions.

rows.label: OR group with an exclusion scoped to the right clause
rows.blind_spot: Without the parentheses the OR binds loosely and the exclusion drifts.

rows.label: Contradictory constraints must return nothing, not a guess
rows.blind_spot: Expected count is zero. Surface the conflict; never drop a constraint to force results.
rows.assumption: Mono-black cards cannot be legal in a Simic identity.

rows.label: Self-negating colour request
rows.blind_spot: Expected count is zero. Offer the inline reinterpretation, do not rewrite.

rows.label: One row per card, not per printing
rows.blind_spot: unique:cards hides printing differences that price and set rows depend on.
rows.assumption: The deckbuilding default. Without it, reprints repeat.

rows.label: Most-played first (Commander)
rows.blind_spot: Popularity is not quality, and rank excludes basic lands. GOV-15.

rows.label: Least-played cards above a rank threshold
rows.technique: Rank floor as an obscurity proxy
rows.blind_spot: A proxy for obscurity, never proof of hidden quality. CAL-027.
rows.assumption: Higher rank number means less played. [RANK] is an explicit threshold.

rows.label: Top 100 cards overall by play rate
rows.blind_spot: Excludes basic lands by design.

rows.label: Cheapest printing of each matching card
rows.blind_spot: Cheapest print may be a digital or promo record; combine with game:paper.

rows.label: Every printing of one exact card
rows.blind_spot: Exact-name search is case-insensitive but otherwise literal.

rows.label: Every distinct illustration of one card
rows.blind_spot: Art dedupe, not printing dedupe.

rows.label: Membership probe - is this card in my pool?
rows.blind_spot: This is the only sound way to prove inclusion or exclusion. A card missing from a truncated result list is UNKNOWN, not absent.
rows.assumption: Returns 1 if the card is in the pool, 0 if not.

rows.label: Under a price ceiling
rows.blind_spot: A card can be expensive in one printing and cheap in another; pair with cheapest:usd when the intent is 'a copy I can afford'.
rows.assumption: Price is printing-level and moves over time.

rows.label: Mana-cheap, not money-cheap
rows.blind_spot: Never conflate the two senses of cheap. CAL-025 requires exposing both.

rows.label: Commander Game Changers
rows.blind_spot: A classification signal, not a social verdict. not:gamechanger does not mean casual.

rows.label: Exclude Game Changers for a lower bracket
rows.blind_spot: Bracket fit is a table conversation; the list is one input to it.

rows.label: Reserved List cards
rows.blind_spot: Reserved List status drives price, not power.

rows.label: Cards from a set
rows.blind_spot: e: is the printing in that set; in: asks whether the card was ever there.

rows.label: Cards ever printed in a set
rows.blind_spot: Different question from e:. Reconciliation flags conflating them.

rows.label: Exclude anything ever printed in a product
rows.blind_spot: Removes the card entirely, not just that printing.

rows.label: One exact physical card
rows.blind_spot: Add lang: for a non-English copy.

rows.label: New cards since a date, excluding reprints
rows.blind_spot: Not the same as cards that received a new printing after that date.

rows.label: Never reprinted in paper
rows.blind_spot: Digital printings are excluded from the paper counts.

rows.label: Heavily reprinted cards
rows.blind_spot: A proxy for staple status at best.

rows.label: Exclude Universes Beyond
rows.blind_spot: Excludes the card, not merely the UB printing.

rows.label: Paper-only Commander pool
rows.blind_spot: game:paper is availability, not legality. Keep both filters.

rows.label: Prefer the cheapest paper printing
rows.blind_spot: prefer: changes which printing is shown, not which cards match.

rows.label: Cards illustrated by an artist
rows.blind_spot: Printing-level.

rows.label: Art containing a subject
rows.blind_spot: Art tags describe the illustration, never the card's function.

rows.label: Flavour text mentions something
rows.blind_spot: Printing-level; reprints differ.

rows.label: Cards with a watermark
rows.blind_spot: Printing-level.

rows.label: Multiple illustrations exist
rows.blind_spot: Card history, not a single printing.

rows.label: Printings in a language
rows.blind_spot: lang:any widens to every language at once.

rows.label: Ever printed in a language
rows.blind_spot: Different from lang:, which is the printing in front of you.

rows.label: Reveal normally hidden records
rows.blind_spot: include: is the one keyword that cannot be negated.
rows.assumption: Vanguard, plane, scheme, phenomenon and memorabilia are hidden by default.

rows.blind_spot: Oracle recall form; confirm the creature itself produces the mana.

rows.blind_spot: Destination matters - battlefield, hand or top of library are different effects. Basic versus nonbasic also matters.

rows.label: Green creature ramp
rows.blind_spot: Uses c: rather than id<= because the proven case asked for green cards, not a green deck's pool.

rows.label: Sol Ring-like acceleration in an identity
rows.query: id<=[COLORS] mv<=2 (o:"additional mana" or o:"search" o:"land" or o:"add ")

rows.blind_spot: One-shot by nature. Distinguish from repeatable production in results.

rows.label: Cost reduction

rows.blind_spot: Finds X in the mana cost. Misses variable effects without X in the cost.

rows.label: Devotion contributors

rows.label: Semantic card advantage (Tagger)
rows.blind_spot: Card advantage is wider than drawing - impulse, recursion and tutoring count. Do not equate the two.

rows.label: Repeatable draw engines on permanents
rows.blind_spot: Repeatable versus one-shot is a card-level classification, not something the query can prove. Label engines after retrieval.

rows.blind_spot: Three templates are needed because a quoted phrase cannot span the variable number. CAL-009.

rows.label: Artifact draw
rows.blind_spot: Independent o: terms can match in unrelated abilities. CAL-010.

rows.label: Cheap creatures that replace themselves
rows.query: t:creature mv<=2 pow<=2 o:"enters" o:"draw a card"
rows.blind_spot: Uses o:"enters", the current Oracle wording. The pre-2024 phrase 'enters the battlefield' no longer matches.

rows.label: Spellslinger cantrips
rows.query: id<=[COLORS] (t:instant or t:sorcery) mv=1 (o:"draw a card" or o:"draw cards")
rows.blind_spot: Cantrip is a curve-and-effect convention, not a rules term.

rows.label: Group hug - everyone draws
rows.blind_spot: Symmetry is the point here; check who benefits more.

rows.blind_spot: Requires discard to appear before draw in the text. Not every match is a classic wheel, and order-reversed wording is missed. CAL-013.

rows.label: Punish only extra draws
rows.query: o:"draws a card" o:"except the first"
rows.blind_spot: Narrow by design - this is the 'every draw after the first' family.

rows.label: Broad removal (Tagger)
rows.fallback: f:commander id<=[COLORS] (o:"destroy target" or o:"exile target")
rows.blind_spot: Functional breadth is intentionally wider than destroy-or-exile wording: bounce, -X/-X, sacrifice and damage all count.

rows.query: id<=[COLORS] t:instant mv<=[MV] (o:"destroy target" or o:"exile target" or o:"gets -")
rows.technique: Identity + speed + curve + three removal templates
rows.blind_spot: Includes -X/-X via o:"gets -", which the destroy-or-exile pair misses.

rows.label: Exile-specifically removal
rows.blind_spot: Oracle verbs do not imply zone. 'Exile target' alone is not guaranteed battlefield removal. CAL-021.

rows.label: Destroy or exile a creature
rows.blind_spot: Misses sacrifice, damage, -X/-X, bounce and non-targeted removal.

rows.label: Artifact and enchantment removal
rows.technique: Alternation on both object and verb
rows.blind_spot: Misses 'destroy target permanent' which also answers the need.

rows.blind_spot: Misses sacrifice-based and exile-based land denial.

rows.blind_spot: Catches intervening restrictions like noncreature or nonland. Misses effects that counter without this template.

rows.query: id<=[COLORS] (o:"counter that spell" or o:"counter it unless" or o:"counter all")

rows.query: id<=[COLORS] (t:artifact or t:enchantment or t:creature) (o:"sacrifice a creature:" or o:"sacrifice another creature:")

rows.blind_spot: This is the outlet lens only. The full archetype needs payoffs and fodder as separate searches. CAL-043.

rows.blind_spot: A trait fingerprint, not similarity. Never search the reference card's name or type as a proxy. CAL-028.

rows.blind_spot: Subject direction matters.

rows.label: Token creators
rows.blind_spot: Creation wording only. A bare o:token mention includes payoffs and spenders, which is a different question. CAL-033. Note otag:token-generator does not exist - probed, zero results.

rows.blind_spot: The exclusion is the whole point and must not be dropped.

rows.blind_spot: Payoff and producer are different roles bundled here; offer role chips.

rows.blind_spot: Distinct from extra turns.
